School shootings are tragedies, but disarming law-abiding citizens isn’t the solution. The real issue? Bloated bureaucracies failing to secure schools while pushing ineffective gun control. Take Georgia’s $21k per-school safety grants—money vanishes into consultants and panic buttons instead of hardening campuses.

Mental health? Existing programs like the 2024 red flag laws haven’t stopped violence because D.C. prioritizes optics over actual security. More hearings mean more bureaucracy, not protection.

The real issue? Big Pharma’s chokehold on Washington. Medical innovation thrives, but corporate monopolies and rigged contracts inflate prices while bureaucrats cash in. The ACA’s expiring tax credits expose a broken system built on subsidies, not solutions.

The Health Care Affordability Act perpetuates the same failed ACA subsidy model that’s already buried taxpayers under $1.7 trillion in healthcare spending since 2010. Expanding premium tax credits to higher income brackets (up to 400% of poverty level) through H.R. 4849 isn’t “lowering costs”—it’s inflating a broken system.

The Congressional Budget Office scored similar bills as adding $210B to the deficit over a decade while doing nothing to rein in hospital price gouging or Big Pharma’s monopoly pricing.

Real reform starts with dismantling ACA bureaucracy, not expanding its reach.

Another week of D.C. theatrics. Expanding SNAP without tackling inflation’s root causes? Recipe for dependency, not solutions. The School Violence Prevention Act (H.R. redacted) throws cash at "trauma-informed" bureaucracy while ignoring real security—like hardening schools against threats.

And the NDAA? More cash for Pentagon desk-jockeys instead of frontline readiness.

Priorities upside down: fund American strength, not feel-good programs.

The FAMILY Act is another D.C. scheme to expand bureaucracy while pretending to help workers. H.R. 3089—the More Paid Leave for More Americans Act—proves the scam: $39.8M in 2026 alone for state grants, software purchases, and "outreach" that'll line consultants' pockets. Section 101(e)(3) funnels cash to "covered partnerships" with private insurers, creating permanent middlemen instead of letting employers handle leave directly.

Meanwhile, Title II's Interstate Paid Leave Action Network demands $8.8M annually for meetings and reports—not actual benefits. Real solution? Cut payroll taxes so workers keep more income upfront instead of laundering their money through 12 layers of federal administration.

Trump's tax cuts put $2K/year back in family budgets—this bill would claw it back through forced "premiums." Prioritize paychecks over paperwork.
